stumbles.quote: Lock your phone's screen rotation in portrait. The game asks for landscape itself, with a prompt telling you when to turn the phone.
stumbles.why: Seems contradictory: with rotation locked in portrait, it's unclear how turning the phone to landscape would work or how the game can display in landscape. The text doesn't explain how the lock and the landscape request fit together.

stumbles.quote: The first screen is held in portrait, and it has the race options:
stumbles.why: Unclear whether the phone is held in portrait or the screen is locked to portrait, and it sits awkwardly with the later landscape turn. It also doesn't say when the prompt appears (after Start engine?).
No options or range are given for Laps (or Difficulty), unlike Track, so it's unclear whether these are numbers, sliders, or presets.
The levels aren't listed, and the text doesn't say what difficulty changes.

stumbles.quote: Top of the phone away from you
stumbles.why: In landscape, "top" is ambiguous: it could mean the edge that was the top in portrait or the edge that is now uppermost. The direction of tilt is hard to work out.
It doesn't say which axis or edge to tilt in landscape (rolling the phone like a steering wheel?), nor how that differs from the accelerate/brake tilt.

stumbles.quote: Tilt Rally runs in a phone browser
stumbles.why: No browser is specified and the iOS prompt is mentioned only vaguely. Nothing covers Android permissions, or what happens if motion access is denied.

point: Open the link on a phone with a motion sensor, pick a track, laps and difficulty, tap Start engine, turn to landscape when prompted, and steer by tilting. The neutral position is set when the lights go out. The orientation instructions are confusing.
